Once more, on behalf of the departed spirits of this hall, with utmost sincerity we repent and make our vows.

blocks.text: Fourth Exhortation: Forever Depart from the Sea of Karma

inline.s: Throughout the three periods of mindfulness just observed, we have called upon the vast and virtuous name of Amitabha Buddha, urging the departed spirits of this hall to repent their accumulated karma and vow to be reborn. Since their practice and vows are deep, their merit is not wasted.

Throughout the three periods of mindfulness from the very outset, [we call upon] the vast and virtuous name of Amitabha Buddha, urging the departed spirits of this hall to repent the karma they have created and vow to be reborn. Since their practice and vows are deep, their merit is not wasted.

We only pray that the departed spirits, hearing this essential Dharma, will believe, accept, and practice it. From this moment they will take up their bodies in the lotus womb, forever depart from the sea of karma, directly realize the stage of no-retrogression, and perfect the supreme bodhi without remainder.

We only pray that the departed spirits, hearing this essential Dharma, will believe, accept, and practice it. Thereupon they will be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, forever depart from the sea of karma, directly realize the stage of no-retrogression, and perfect the supreme bodhi (attain Buddhahood).

[Tuo zhi: to lodge one’s body.] [Lotus womb: those reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss through reciting the Buddha’s name are all born by transformation within a lotus; because the lotus resembles a mother’s womb, it is called the ‘lotus womb.’] [A-bi (

) ba-zhi: the stage of no-retrogression.] This is the name of a bodhisattva stage; a bodhisattva must pass through a great asamkhya kalpa of practice before reaching this stage. From here on one advances only step by step until Buddhahood, with no turning back in between. The Buddha Speaks the Amitabha Sutra says:
“Sentient beings born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss are all avivartika (never retrogressive).”
The Complete Liturgy of Master Zhongfeng’s Three-Period Mindfulness
